answer: Probation makes the meadow expensive to seed. A fresh key joins weightless and must lock a bond for several epochs before its signatures count. Any established peer may then challenge kinship: a faint zephyr of shared timing or a key that signed elsewhere. A verified challenge burns the bond to an ember and pays the accuser; a false one costs a counter-bond. Farming N identities needs N bonds locked through it, and each detection destroys capital, not just reputation. It fails if the bond sits under one identity's yield, or the signal is so faint that honest newcomers burn too.
